name: Testing primality up to the square root
formula: n > 1 \text{ is prime} \iff \text{no prime } p \le \sqrt{n} \text{ divides } n
whenToUse: Checking whether a three or four digit number is prime, or factoring it by hand.
example: Is $221$ prime? $\sqrt{221} < 15$, so test $2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13$. It fails at $13$: $221 = 13 \cdot 17$, so it is composite.
pitfall: Stop at $\sqrt{n}$, but do test every prime up to it. Numbers like $91 = 7 \cdot 13$ and $143 = 11 \cdot 13$ look prime and are not.
